articles.title: Six Nations: No plans for Ireland Six Nations game in US - IRFU
articles.summary: There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says.
articles.body:
There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says.

World Rugby's chief executive Alan Gilpin said on Wednesday that it would help any nation that wants to switch a Six Nations match to the US, as it continues its drive to spread the game stateside.

He used the example of Ireland v Italy as a game that would resonate with expatriate fans in the United States and could help the sport further establish itself there.

But, in a statement issued on Friday, the IRFU dismissed the idea that it was considering moving any fixtures to the US.

"The United States is an important growth market for rugby and we welcome and embrace initiatives that help introduce the sport to new audiences and, crucially, generate new revenues for the game," said an IRFU spokesperson.

"There are currently no plans or discussions, from an IRFU perspective, regarding Six Nations matches being played in the United States.

"We believe the Six Nations holds a special place for supporters across all participating unions, and the opportunity for fans in Ireland and Italy to support their teams at home remains a central part of the competition's appeal."

Switch Six Nations fixture to USA to grow game – World Rugby

In an interview with the Daily Telegraph , external and The Times , external , Gilpin said: "This isn't a live discussion of an Italy v Ireland game, but why we use that as an example is because you've got two fantastic fanbases in the US of Irish and Italian fans.

"If you could take a Six Nations game to the right place, to a Boston or to a New York, where there's a lot of those fanbases, you can definitely drive the economics.

"Now, you're going to have Irish fans and Italian fans in those respective home countries saying: 'Hang on a minute, you know, we want to see our country play?'

"The counter-argument to that [is] it's still Irish and Italian fans getting the chance to watch their team, so they're just not the ones who live in Ireland and Italy on this occasion. But that's a balancing piece we've got to work through."

Ireland have previously enjoyed two well-attended games in the US against New Zealand.

They memorably beat the All Blacks for the first time when the teams met in front of a capacity 60,000-strong crowd at Chicago's Soldier Field in 2016 , with a 2025 rematch which they lost also proving a similar commercial success.

articles.title: England v Australia: Natasha Hunt zeroing in on Lions opportunity
articles.summary: England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says the inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour to New Zealand - the first Test of which is exactly a year away today - is a massive motivation as she prepares to make her comeback from injury.
articles.body:
England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says the inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour to New Zealand - the first Test of which is exactly a year away - is a massive motivation as she prepares to make her comeback from injury.

The 37-year-old sustained knee ligament damage during England's Six Nations opener against Ireland in April.

She was sidelined for the rest of the Red Roses' Grand-Slam winning campaign and Gloucester-Hartpury's run to the PWR semi-finals, but starts at nine in England's WXV Global Series opener against Australia in Salford on Saturday.

"I've been fortunate enough to have played in Team GB Sevens set-ups twice over," said Hunt, a veteran of the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2021 Olympics.

"That was some of my favourite, most enjoyable rugby, just mixing cultures, everyone having a common goal and coming together really quickly to try to get something special done.

"It would be unbelievable to be involved in [the Lions tour].

"I think every player that is close to playing for their country in those four nations is thinking about it. And if they say they're not, they're lying!"

The landmark five-fixture tour begins on 4 September with a warm-up fixture against a Black Ferns XV, before the first of three Tests against New Zealand seven days later.

Coach Jo Yapp is expected to name her squad in May 2027, after the conclusion of next year's Women's Six Nations.

Hunt spent much of the past summer working with Gloucester's strength and conditioning team to rehabilitate her knee and, after seeing Lucy Packer impress in her absence, has got the nod to start against the Wallaroos.

Hunt forms a half-back partnership with Holly Aitchison. The pair first played together almost a decade ago, when Aitchison was a fast-rising teenage prospect at Litchfield Ladies.

"We played one game together - I was nine, she was 10 against Worcester and we really enjoyed it," remembers Hunt.

"She's just such an exciting rugby player. Her ability to play at the line is pretty unmatched in the game.

"The way that she can take a ball at such pace, challenge that line and then fizz a pass 20 metres... I don't think there's many people in the game that can do that."

After taking on Australia, who they beat 47-7 en route to winning the World Cup last year, England face Canada and New Zealand on the following two weekends.

The second half of the WXV Global Series takes the Red Roses across the Atlantic in October for a match against the USA and a two-Test series against Canada.

articles.title: Super League: Wigan 50-12 Catalans Dragons - Warriors win sixth League Leaders' Shield
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors win a sixth League Leaders' Shield as they beat Catalans Dragons to wrap up top spot in Super League heading into the play-offs.
articles.body:
Tries: Smith, Marshall 2, O'Neill, Farrell, Daniel, Field, Eckersley, Keighran Goals: Keighran 7

Tries: Tison, Lis Goals: Aispuro-Bichet, Garcia

Wigan Warriors won a sixth League Leaders' Shield as they ran in nine tries to beat Catalans Dragons and carry on their remarkable run of form heading into the Super League play-offs.

Matt Peet's side, who were trophyless in 2025 off the back of their quadruple-winning 2024 campaign, have now won two pieces of silverware, having lifted the Challenge Cup in May, and are now two games away from a treble.

Harry Smith and Ugo Tison exchanged tries early on, but Liam Marshall, Brad O'Neill and Liam Farrell put Wigan in control at the break.

Austin Daniel and Jai Field continued Wigan's scoring streak, while Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran and Marshall's second wrapped up a thumping 16th win in a row, with Alexis Lis scoring a fine consolation try for Les Dracs in the closing stages.

Despite Friday's victory ensuring the shield was theirs, the really hard work was done in last week's crucial win over title rivals Leeds Rhinos at Headingley, where they leapfrogged their rivals to go top.

Had Wigan have lost then, Leeds could have pulled off a dramatic final-day surge back to the top, winning the shield at their expense on points difference, but the Rhinos fell short and were beaten by Hull FC on Friday.

Wigan now have a bye week by virtue of a top two place and will be at home for their Super League play-off semi-final on Saturday, 26 September, live on the BBC.

For Catalans, it means a difficult campaign ends with a ninth-placed finish. Les Dracs have now not made the end-of-season play-offs since their run to the Super League Grand Final in 2023 - where they were also beaten by Wigan.

Poor Leeds stunned by impressive Hull FC

For Wigan, winning the Shield is the culmination of a remarkable turnaround in form having been sixth in the table during a controversial and heavy 62-4 defeat away to Hull KR in May in the lead-up to the Challenge Cup final.

That defeat was their fifth in nine games, but since that point they have won all 16 games, beginning with their triumph at Wembley against the Robins.

There were tributes pre-match to captain Farrell, who announced he will retire at the end of the season, as Wigan's players warmed up with t-shirts emblazoned with Faz 12.

The hosts got off to the perfect start as Smith sold a perfect dummy to glide through the Catalans' defence to score, but that lead was cut back thanks to Tison's impressive solo effort soon after.

Marshall cantered in at the corner to put Wigan back ahead, while O'Neill spotted a gap to go through, and Farrell saw the half out having returned from a shoulder injury which had left him on the sidelines since June.

Daniel's easy run-in on the wing got Wigan going after the break before Field raced in from Farrell's offload to continue the rout.

Eckersley's 27th try of the season sent Wigan further ahead as he showed great intelligence to race through, while Keighran matched his fine work with the boot with a long-range run-in of his own. Marshall barged through for his second - leaving Farrell to take, and subsequently miss, the conversion.

Fellow retiree Ben Garcia did succeed with the boot, however, as he kicked the extras in the aftermath of Lis' try on the verge of the full-time hooter.

'Emotions were part of the challenge' - reaction

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet told BBC Radio Manchester:

"It was a fantastic night. A bit surreal. It went really well, particularly Liam [Farrell] scoring that try and the part he played. And I think we've come through healthy.

"I think Catalans were here to play but ultimately we got the job done.

"A lot of emotion, that was part of the challenge tonight to put that to one side and be clinical with our performance and I was very proud of the group and the staff."

[On this season] "So far so good but it's not without its challenges and hopefully those challenges bring us through in good stead, and whether we get the job done or not, we have a good group here."

articles.title: Super League: Leeds Rhinos 12-18 Hull FC - Black and Whites claim stunning win
articles.summary: Lowly Hull FC stun second-placed Leeds Rhinos to end a dire Super League season in style.
articles.body:
Tries: Hankinson, Watkins Goals: Connor 2

Lowly Hull FC stunned second-placed Leeds Rhinos to end a dire Super League season in style.

The result, coupled with Wigan Warriors' thumping 50-12 win over Catalans Dragons, saw Matt Peet's men claim the League Leaders' Shield.

Hull FC have endured an incredibly difficult 2026 but took a deserved lead through Logan Moy's score before Chris Hankinson's try made it 6-6 at the break.

Lloyd Kemp put the Black and Whites back in front after Leeds failed with a short drop-out and, after the home side blew chances to level the scores with handling errors, Lennon Clark went over.

Kallum Watkins set up a big finish with a try with three minutes to go but the hard-working visitors held out for a shock win.

Brad Arthur's Leeds side were badly disjointed in attack throughout against a team who had won seven of 26 games going into Friday's meeting and have now lost four of their past nine games.

They will have two weeks to stew on this result before hosting their play-off semi-final on Friday, 25 September.

Wigan beat Catalans to win sixth League Leaders' Shield

Warrington pass feisty Toulouse test to seal third place

Wakefield see off Leigh to confirm home play-off

Lomax and Percival shine as Saints beat Hull KR

It has been a year to forget for Hull FC.

Head coach John Cartwright left in acrimonious circumstances in March after being told his contract would not be extended beyond this season, with the club appointing former England coach Steve McNamara to take over for 2027.

Andy Last was placed in interim charge but the season crumbled to the extent that, amid a 12-match losing run, the owners issued a statement in July to apologise to the club's fans.

However, this win over an admittedly out-of-sorts Leeds will give players, fans and incoming coach McNamara hope for the future.

Their three tries came from young home grown players in Kemp, 19, and Moy and Clark, both 21, and they showed a grit in defence that had been lacking for all too much of this season.

Victory also saw retiring club legend Tom Briscoe go out in style in what was his 400th and final Super League appearance.

Leeds welcomed back the league's leading try-scorer Maika Sivo after two months out with a broken arm but he, like his team-mates, was way below his best.

The Rhinos went unbeaten at Headingley until August but have now lost their past three games in front of their own fans.

A fourth straight loss in their upcoming semi-final would see a campaign that had promised so much fall short of the Grand Final.

'Result nothing short of amazing' - reaction

Leeds head coach Brad Arthur told BBC Radio Leeds:

"I thought we dominated field position and possession, I just thought we were poor on our edges with our execution. We created more than enough opportunities and we didn't ice them.

"The forwards couldn't have done any more. We kicked when we should have passed, passed when we should have kicked or there was poor selection with the pass, poor catch. Our skill level wasn't good enough.

"We lacked urgency. They scored from a drop-out. That isn't good enough.

"Our last two weeks haven't been great but in 14 days that isn't going to count for anything really. We've got five or six sessions leading into the game to recover and make sure everyone knows what their job is.

"We are 80 minutes from Old Trafford and we've got to get it right."

Hull FC interim head coach Andy Last told BBC Radio Humberside:

"Outstanding. 18-12 away to Leeds on the back of them hurting after losing in a big game to Wigan, to come up with the effort and the performance and that result is nothing short of amazing.

"They dominated position and possession and we consistently turned them away. Our spirit, our desire and our grit and determination was evident for everyone to see. It's a fantastic way to finish the season.

"I'm absolutely not sad [the season is over]. It's been very challenging mentally, emotionally and physically for myself. That game probably typifies the season that we've had - you just don't know what you are going to get from this Hull FC group."

articles.title: England 48-15 Australia: Red Roses' seven-try second-half blitz earns win in WXV Global Series opener
articles.summary: Seven tries in the second half saw England open their WXV Global series with a win over Australia; Next, England meet Canada in a repeat of their 2025 World Cup final at Sandy Park in Exeter on September 19; they round off the home leg of the series against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium
articles.body:
Despite a scintillating second 40 from the hosts, the first half was all about Australia as they showed defensive strength to hold on to a 10-5 lead at half-time thanks to a Samantha Wood penalty and a converted Faliki Pohiva effort.

When Wood was in the sin bin for a deliberate knock on was the only time the Red Roses got on the board as Abi Burton went over from short range. Holly Aitchison was unable to add the extras.

Remarkably, it was the first time the Red Roses had trailed at half-time in seven years, the last time coming all the way back in 2019.

However, it was in the second half that England got back to their usual best and with tries from May Campbell, Meg Jones, Bryony Field, Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer, Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, plus a conversion from Holly Aitchison and three from Zoe Harrison, they made it 39 matches in a row unbeaten.

The Wallaroos did get a second-half try thorugh Eva Karpani, who was earlier sent to the sin bin for an infringement in the build-up to Venner's try but it was merely a consolation as the Red Roses showed just why they are currently the No 1 ranked team and world champions.

Next up for England is Canada on September 19 in Exeter, before they face New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on September 26.

A second-half serving of Red Roses running wild

It was truly a tale of two halves in the North West of England as Australia took an early lead after England were penalised for holding on, Wood slotting over the conversion for a three-point lead after four minutes.

The Red Roses thought they had quickly hit back through skipper Meg Jones but on review, she was offside as the charge down on the kick occurred and so her effort was chalked off, and the visitors' early advantage was reinstated.

Despite Australia taking control, they allowed England to get into the game when Wood was sent to the sin bin for a deliberate knock on and they had to battle for 10 minutes with just 14 players.

They did well for five minutes until the Red Roses' numerical advantage brought the spoils on the left edge, Sadia Kabeya passing back on the inside to send Burton in.

That did not deter Australia though and back at full strength, they thought they had gone over through Brittany Merlo but once again the video referee intervened and this time dismissed the try due to sealing off at the line-out.

It took eight minutes for the Wallaroos to go over again and this time it was from an impressive steal at the line-out. Off the back of it, Pohiva used her strength to burrow over and Wood converted to put Australia 10-5 ahead.

Australia's defence, as it did throughout the majority of the first half, then continued to stand firm and deny England any more points before the break. That meant they went in behind for the first time in seven years and were firmly in unprecedented territory.

That seemed to motivate the home side though and it took seven minutes for England to pull the line-out maul out of their back pocket with Campbell finishing it off. This time, Aitchison converted for a 12-10 lead.

Four tries in 10 minutes saw England find their electric best in attack and take the game away from Australia.

On the 51st minute, skipper Jones finished off a brilliant Aitchison kick. On the 55th minute, debutante Field steered the driving maul over. On the 57th minute, Venner went over in the corner and then on the 61st minute, Kabeya forced her way over under the posts to cap off a relentless period.

This time, Harrison added the conversion to put England 34-10 up with less than 20 minutes remaining.

During that pressure, things went from bad to worse for Australia as they had Karpani sin-binned for an infringement during the build-up to Venner's try and of course, England were not done adding points to their tally.

Replacement No 7 Packer then got in on the actions as she used the breakdown in her favour to get over, Harrison accurate with the boot once again to put the Red Roses 41-10 up.

On her return from a 10-minute sit down, Karpani did manage to hit back for Australia as she crashed over from the back of the lineout.

However, England made sure to have the last word as Moloney-MacDonald showed her speed on the edge, Harrison capping off the afternoon with a brilliant touchline conversion to see the game finish 48-15.

Player of the Match Abi Burton told BBC Sport:

"It was tough, they made us work for it. We knew we weren't at our best at half-time, we needed to come out and bring it to them physically because they came out absolutely gunning.

"That cohesiveness started to click at the end. There is so much more to come from this team, we've just got a few teething issues to sort out.

"It's going to take time for us to get back into it with a shorter pre-season. But it's about how we adapt quickly and great ready for the next Test match.

"We're a different group of players in some aspects, but the messages have always been the same: be the best versions of ourselves and be as cohesive as possible. It's an ever-evolving Red Roses team."

articles.title: South Africa vs New Zealand: Springboks show steel to secure 43-28 victory and 3-1 series win against All Blacks
articles.summary: South Africa entered the fourth Test with a 2-1 lead over New Zealand in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series; They increased that to 3-1 with a 43-28 victory at the home of NFL's Baltimore Ravens
articles.body:
South Africa had a narrow 17-14 half-time lead thanks to a Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu penalty plus converted tries from Damien De Allende and Morné van den Berg.

However, New Zealand had scored early through Cody Taylor and then hit again late on through Will Jordan, Damian McKenzie converting both to put his side just three points adrift with 40 minutes to play.

The game looked in the balance in the second half after converted tries from Malcolm Marx and Steph du Toit were met by an Ethan Blackadder effort.

However, Kurt-Lee Arendse took his opportunity to race away and score and was quickly followed up by Cameron Hanekom to seal a Springboks win, a Beauden Barrett late try merely a consolation.

Indeed, the Springboks took the win in front of the largest attendance ever at a rugby union match in the United States.

New Zealand went 1-0 up after a 33-16 win at Johannesburg's Ellis Park but then the Springboks hit back in the next two Tests. They won 33-26 in Cape Town and followed that up with a close 29-24 win at Soweto's FNB Stadium.

That meant Rugby's Greatest Rivalry had a grand finale in Baltimore which saw the Springboks prevail in the first traditional series between the two sides in 30 years.

Not only that, it was a victory that marked head coach Rassie Erasmus' 100th Test in charge.

USA sets stage for a Test to remember between two powerhouses

After a spine-tingling Haka from the All Blacks, the Baltimore crowd erupted as this fourth and final Test of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series got under way.

There was some early ill-discipline from both sides but as the game settled, and after an early Feinberg-Mngomezulu penalty, it was the All Blacks that crossed the whitewash first.

Some sensationally slick hands out to left edge opened the space for Taylor to run a fantastic line and score, McKenzie converting for a 7-3 lead.

The possession then all went in favour of the Springboks for much of the rest of the half. Poor handling from New Zealand gave away opportunities and off the back of a scrum, South Africa continuously powered over the gain line until De Allende eventually barrelled over and with the conversion, they had a 10-7 advantage after a breathless first 15 minutes.

After a brief break to fix a communication issue for the refereeing team, the game got back under way and South Africa pounced again on the 22nd minute. Off the back off the driving maul from five metres out Van den Berg through a delicious dummy to score.

Once again, the try was converted and it looked like South Africa had a comprehensive 17-7 lead. Frankly, they could have had more if they iced all their opportunities.

However, New Zealand were not done and just three minutes before half-time, and after 32 phases, the gap opened for Jordan to run through and score under the sticks for his 55th Test try.

The conversion from McKenzie had the game finely balanced at 17-14 with just 40 minutes of rugby remaining in this series.

South Africa made dominance pay in the second half when, off the back of a driving maul, Marx barrelled over and was quickly followed by Du Toit within the space of three minutes. Van den Berg converted the second try and with less than half an hour remaining, the Springboks had a 29-14 lead.

The All Blacks hit back through an Ethan Blackadder converted try which seemed to have the game finely poised at 29-21.

But, just as New Zealand looked to be firing in attack once again to race away and score, a knock on provided Arendse with an opportunity to show off his silky foot work, race away, and dive in under the sticks.

New Zealand's bubble was then firmly burst as, just four minutes later, Hanekom went over to make sure the series would go South Africa's way. Libbok converted both and a 43-21 lead looked enough.

Beauden Barrett did manage to add a late consolation try but it was merely that as South Africa showed once again why they are the No 1 team in world rugby.

South Africa captain Siya Kolisi speaking on Sky Sports...

"I want to thank every South African here in the stadium and back at home.

"It was a special week to see you come out in umbers and support us. We are so grateful.

"We could hear you today. Thank you so much.

"To the New Zealand supporters too, thank you for coming to our beautiful country and embracing our culture.

"We go hard on each other on the field but the respect we have for each other is always there."

articles.title: England 48-15 Australia: Red Roses win WXV Global Series opener
articles.summary: England produce dominant second-half performance to comfortably defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series.
articles.body:
Tries: Burton, Campbell, Jones, Field, Venner, Kabeya, L Packer, Moloney-MacDonald Cons: Aitchison, Harrison 3

Tries: Pohiva, Karpani Con: Wood Pen: Wood

England produced a dominant second-half performance to defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series.

The world champions, playing their first game since winning a record eighth successive Women's Six Nations title in May, were made to work for victory in Salford after trailing at half-time for the first time since 2020.

The Wallaroos led 10-5 at the break, with player of the match Abi Burton scoring England's only try in an error-strewn first half.

John Mitchell's side responded emphatically after the interval, scoring seven tries to quickly put any prospect of a shock defeat to bed and extend their record winning run to 39 matches in front of a crowd of 9,251.

The England head coach described the fixture as "a good pre-season game" after it kicked off the 2026-27 campaign for his players.

"It was the first pre-season game of the year where we had the reality of playing rugby and had to solve [problems], which is good for us," Mitchell told BBC Sport.

"It is an absolute joke if you are worried about being down 10-5. More important is how we worked our way back into it.

"We got 23 players with rugby [into them], and it was a 43-point second half."

During a dominant 20-minute spell, May Campbell, captain Meg Jones, Bryony Field, Mia Venner and Sadia Kabeya all crossed for tries.

Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald also then scored, with Australia's Asoiva Karpani adding to Faliki Pohiva's first-half try.

The WXV Global Series has replaced the WXV competition, with England having won both editions of the premier section, WXV1, in 2023 and 2024.

Running from 2026 to 2028, the series features the world's top 12 teams and is designed to provide more competitive matches before the 2029 World Cup in Australia.

The Red Roses face Canada at Exeter's Sandy Park next weekend, the teams' first meeting since England won last year's Rugby World Cup final, before facing New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on 26 September.

"They're great rivals [Canada], a fantastic rugby team, well-coached, a different team to Australia," Mitchell added.

"We only have a very short turnaround. With this being our first pre-season game, lots of players got rugby, so we'll be in a great place."

England blitz Australia in second half to maintain winning run - reaction & try clips

This was the first game with the new women's size 4.5 ball, which is 3% smaller than the standard size five.

In May, England fly-half Zoe Harrison, arguably the best goal-kicker in the women's game, said introducing the ball was "the worst decision someone has ever made".

Scrum-half Samantha Wood confidently drilled over an early penalty as Australia, like they did against England in Brighton in last year's World Cup, started quicker.

Sloppy handling and inaccuracy in the Wallaroos' 22 held back Mitchell's side in the first half.

Burton's try came from slick handling and interplay, indicating what new attack coach Emily Scarratt is trying to implement, even if England were not at their brightest early on.

"The message at half-time was we know that we weren't at our best, so we knew we needed to come out and rip back into them and give it to them physically because they came out absolutely gunning," Burton told BBC Sport.

"At the end that cohesiveness started to kick in.

"There's so much more to come from this team, just a few teething issues we needed to sort out."

Both sides had tries disallowed in the first half, but Australia scrambled brilliantly in defence to take a deserved lead into the break.

The Red Roses have often started slowly under Mitchell before clicking into gear, with the power of their bench a level above the rest.

However, England had not trailed at half-time since a match against France in November 2020.

Red Roses turn to power to avoid shock defeat

Mitchell said that, without a "tournament to win", his side have to be "very patient" in how they approach these Test matches.

With a shock defeat potentially looming, his side turned to their destructive maul to power over the line before a scrum penalty gave them valuable field position.

A clever grubber kick from Sale Sharks' Holly Aitchison, on her 50th cap, then found Jones as the combination of power and backline skill finally came together.

When in need of a try, the Red Roses maul tends to deliver more often than not.

It was England's pack that dominated Canada to win the World Cup, and it delivered again through Field to give them some breathing room.

England, with the likes of Hannah Botterman and Marlie Packer coming off the bench, continued to grow into the game as their accuracy improved while Australia tired.

Both wingers crossed to underline the balance in play that has made Mitchell's side so difficult to beat.

Harrison also nailed three conversions, underlining a successful adjustment to the new ball.

Both Canada and New Zealand will pose more of a threat in attack and will take note of how Australia made life difficult for the Red Roses in the first half.

But it is yet another win for a side who, simply put, seem to know little else.

articles.title: Scotland 26-64 Canada: Ruthless visitors outclass Scots in WXV opener
articles.summary: Canada prove too strong for Scotland as they score 10 tries to register a resounding win in their WXV Series opener in Edinburgh.
articles.body:
Tries : Gallagher, Campbell, Skeldon, Lloyd Cons : Nelson 3

Tries : Gibson 2, Apps 2, Kassil, Omokhuale, Perry, Pelletier, Senft, Bauder Cons : Gallagher 7

World Cup finalists Canada proved too strong for Scotland as they ran in 10 tries to register a resounding win in their WXV Series opener in Edinburgh.

Canada struck early when a brilliant offload from hooker Kiki Idowu found Rachel Smith on the charge and left the Scottish defence scrambling.

The 2025 World Cup runners-up held out for multiple phases on their own line before Lizzie Gibson found the gap to dive over for the opening try.

They quickly scored a second when scrum-half Olivia Apps darted over in the corner.

Scotland needed a response and they got it when Evie Gallagher – on her first Test appearance since last year's World Cup - blasted over from close range to bring the hosts back within five points.

The response was swift, however, as Gibson sliced through for her second try to re-establish Canada's 12-points lead.

Brittanny Kassil – who would receive a 20-minute red card after the break for a high shot on Meryl Smith - and Julia Omokhuale blasted over from close range for two tries in quick succession as the Canadians started to flex their muscles.

The Scots gave the home crowd something to cheer with their second try.

Debutant Rhea Clarke did brilliantly to strip opposite number Apps in contact. She set Gallagher free and she held off two tackles before finding Shona Campbell on her shoulder to score.

Fly-half Taylor Perry extinguished any hopes of a Scottish fightback as she sliced through the midfield untouched for Canada's sixth try early in the second half.

The Scots were tiring and Apps carved them open with a lovely little show-and-go to streak away and go in under the sticks.

Hooker Lana Skeldon burrowed over for Scotland's third try, but substitute Justine Pelletier responded in kind almost immediately.

Helen Nelson dinked a wonderful little kick over the Canada defence and into the arms of Rhona Lloyd to go over for Scotland's fourth, but Gabrielle Senft powered over and substitute Savannah Bauder scored a fabulous individual try on her Test debut to ensure Canada had the last word.

The Scots face New Zealand at Hive Stadium next Saturday (17:10 BST), while Canada face England at Sandy Park in a re-run of last year's World Cup final on the same day (15:00).

articles.title: South Africa 43-28 New Zealand: Boks complete series victory in Baltimore
articles.summary: South Africa complete a 3-1 series win over New Zealand as the world champions' consistency, power and cohesion proves too much in the fourth Test in Baltimore.
articles.body:
Tries: de Allende (2), van den Berg, PS du Toit, Arendse, Hanekom Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu (2), van den Berg, Libbok (2) Pens: Feinberg-Mngomezulu

Tries: Taylor, Jordan, Blackadder, B Barrett Cons: McKenzie (4)

South Africa completed a 3-1 series win over New Zealand as the world champions' consistency, power and cohesion once again proved too much in the fourth Test in Baltimore.

After victory in the series opener in Johannesburg last month, the All Blacks jumped to the top of the world rankings and threatened to shake up rugby's world order.

However, South Africa clawed their way back to triumph - just as their director of rugby Rassie Erasmus had predicted.

While New Zealand were spirited and skilful in pursuit of a win to square the series, the Springboks' go-forward up front and the depth of their bench kept the All Blacks at bay.

The match played out in front of a near-capacity crowd of 68,173 at the M&T Bank Stadium, the largest-ever crowd to watch a rugby match in the USA.

A successful stateside excursion completes a series that has been compelling viewing and stress-tested both sides' aspirations of lifting the Rugby World Cup next year - the two nations have won the past five editions of the tournament.

It was New Zealand who started fastest in Maryland on Saturday.

Eight minutes in, their breathtakingly quick tiki-taka catch-pass, with the backline holding their depth, outflanked South Africa's blitz defence to set up the first try of the match for hooker Codie Taylor.

However, the Springboks' brute strength in the close quarters meant they could collect points without needing to resort to such high-risk passages of play.

With their forward pack on top in the scrum and winning collisions, Damian de Allende burrowed over from short range, before scrum-half Morne van den Berg flashed a dummy and darted past Sam Darry for a similar score.

Those tries opened up a 17-7 lead for the Springboks. With Eben Etzebeth crunching returning New Zealand fly-half Richie Mo'unga in the tackle and Jasper Wiese stampeding around in the loose, the Boks seemed poised to stretch away and out of sight.

Fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, who had pushed a long-range penalty to the right of the uprights early on, missed a drop-goal shot. An overcooked attempt to find the corner also cost his team.

New Zealand's combination of hard toil and sparkling hands then bought them a way back into the game just before half-time.

Will Jordan, his nation's all-time leading try-scorer, streaked off his wing on a superb line to dunk down over the line at the end of 32 draining phases.

Four points down at the break, Dave Rennie's side had hopes of taking home half of a specially-designed series trophy, which, held together by magnets, can be shared between the two sides.

But South Africa ensured that innovation went unused.

Malcolm Marx trundled over at the back of a rolling maul after the interval and, three minutes later, Pieter-Steph du Toit barged over after a sharp blindside break by the impressive Van den Berg.

Ethan Blackadder's score in the final quarter cut the Boks' lead to eight points, but South Africa hit the accelerator once again as the toll taken by a high-paced match and a long tour caught up on both teams and space opened up.

Kurt-Lee Arendse sliced through open field after Damian McKenzie had broken through in the opposite direction, but Josh Moorby failed to gather his pass.

Four minutes later, Cameron Hanekom scooped up scrappy ball to put the result beyond doubt and render replacement Beauden Barrett's late try only a footnote.

articles.title: Georgia Evans': A title, a ring and an IVF eye opener - Wales forward's whirlwind year
articles.summary: Wales forward Georgia Evans will not forget 2026 - having won a league title, got engaged, bought a house and started the process of having a family.
articles.body:
Wales forward Georgia Evans is smiling from ear to ear as she takes a seat in front of the media, and it is not surprising given the year she has had so far.

While most of us were basking in record breaking temperatures, Evans began her summer by winning the Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) title with Saracens.

A few days later she was proposed to by England World Cup winner Hannah Botterman in front of a dreamy Greek sunset, and now boasts an engagement ring so big it should be classed as a structural hazard.

Throw in a new house, plans to start a family and 2026 will take some beating for the 29-year-old.

Live on BBC One, iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app, with live text coverage

It was around this time 12 months ago when I was interviewing a very different Georgia Evans.

Wales had crashed out of the World Cup in miserable fashion, while Evans' individual appearance was targeted by online trolls, sparking a social media storm.

The rugby community - of course - rallied, with her trademark pink ribbon becoming the tournament's symbol of solidarity.

"This year, I'm in a really good space," said Evans.

"I've got lots of things to focus on outside of rugby and coming into the [Wales] environment, I've just taken the pressure off.

"It's now about being my happiest self and when I'm happy, I'm playing free and the coaches allow me that freedom."

Evans and Botterman may be on opposing sides for club and country, but together they make the perfect team.

Evans said "it's amazing" to support her fiancee and see the success she has with England, who are on a 39-Test winning streak.

"Obviously it makes me a little bit jealous at times, but she's also been through the troubles of injury and rehab," said Evans, who was in the Salford crowd on Saturday to watch Botterman make her comeback in England's victory over Australia.

"To have that connection is pretty special and unique. The fact that we're not in each other's pockets, but doing the same type of thing every day, also really helps.

"I'm incredibly proud of her and I hope she's proud of me."

When asked about her surprise engagement, Evans lit up.

"I was in a bit of a bubble. It felt like a fever dream where you just don't know what's going on, and then I came back for pre-season and it all hits you pretty hard."

She said it was a bit too early to start planning a wedding, but fellow Wales forward Alisha Joyce and Wales centre Meg Webb had both been enlisted as bridesmaids.

"I've allowed them to run with my hen do, so God knows if I'll come back alive," Evans joked.

Evans and Botterman have started the process of planning a family.

Speaking openly on The Good, The Scaz & The Rugby podcast, Botterman said she had been for IVF pre-scans which had left her "terribly surprised".

"It's a bit of an eye opener, all the things you have to go through and put in place," added Evans.

"Unfortunately it's not a happy accident that just happens for us, but it's something that we've looked into for the future."

The couple also praised the support available from their unions. Alisha and wife Jaz Joyce became the first couple to have a baby in Wales' camp, having welcomed their son Ralphie in November.

"Speaking to Hannah and [England head coach] John Mitchell they're absolutely amazing with families and super supportive, so is Lynny (Wales head coach Sean Lynn), he loves the family feel here, baby Ralphie is always around," said Evans.

"It's another step forward to allow us as elite athletes to plan for motherhood because rugby is such a small time frame in your life, and it's such a bigger thing to look forward to after rugby, or during as you've seen with so many incredible women at the moment."

As to the allegiance of any potential children, Evans was quick to respond: "We've already had that argument. They'll be wearing a Welsh shirt for sure."

articles.title: South Africa vs New Zealand: Record crowd in Baltimore provides 'appetiser' for 2031 Rugby World Cup on US soil
articles.summary: The fourth Test in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series between South Africa and New Zealand drew in a record crowd for rugby union on US soil; The teams are hoping it provides a strong start ahead of America hosting the Rugby World Cup in 2031
articles.body:
Saturday's crowd of 68,173 was the largest ever for a rugby international in the US. The colours speckling the stands revealed that most were in the green of South Africa, with a few black jerseys of New Zealand and a balance of interested neutrals.

They enjoyed an enthralling Test in which the Springboks ran out 43-28 winners to clinch a 3-1 series victory.

Rugby has tried for years to break into the lucrative American sporting market. Saturday's large and enthusiastic crowd suggested there might yet be a foothold.

Speaking after the clash, All Blacks captain Codie Taylor and his Springboks counterpart, Siya Kolisi, agreed that giving Americans more opportunities to see rugby is crucial to whetting their appetites for the World Cup they will host in five years.

"It's great to come over here and see what America has to offer," Taylor said. "They love their sports and they got right behind rugby.

"America has obviously got some great sports and they're fanatical about every sport they're involved in. It would be great to see US Rugby keep building.

"Leading into 2031, it's in a strong place to lay the foundation for what will be an awesome World Cup."

Kolisi also was positive about the future for rugby in the country and he hopes NFL teams might adopt the game as an offseason option, investing in existing American clubs.

"I really think Americans would love rugby if they get to see more of it and if it's shown a whole lot more on TV," Kolisi said. But I think it needs a lot of hard work obviously.

"I really believe if the NFL teams buy into rugby and if they become part-owners in the rugby clubs and if some of their players who don't get to play often, if they let them play rugby I think that would help the game a lot.

"Also I think it's a game that Americans would actually enjoy. They love physical sports. So I really think the more teams get to come and play here, the more people are invested in the rugby teams."

Kolisi hails Rassie: He reminds us where we come from

The fourth Test between South Africa and New Zealand marked Rassie Erasmus' 100th Test in charge of the Springoks and Kolisi hailed him as the reason why their side are as dominant as they are.

"We've got coach Rassie (Erasmus)," he said. "He knows us and gets us up. When he speaks to us he reminds us where we come from.

"The players who are in the group but not playing today, we do it for them, the guys who are injured and also for the people of South Africa who would love to have the opportunities we have."

articles.title: Super League Dream Team 2026: Leeds dominate selection with six picks
articles.summary: Leeds Rhinos have six selections in the 2026 Super League Dream Team - more than any other side.
articles.body:
Leeds Rhinos' impressive Super League campaign in finishing second has been reflected in six players selected in the 2026 Dream Team.

Half-backs Jake Connor and Brodie Croft, full-back Lachie Miller, winger Maika Sivo, centre Ash Handley and back-rower James McDonnell were selected in a line-up picked through a process involving journalists, fans and former players.

Wigan, who are two-thirds of the way to a potential treble and have secured the League Leaders' Shield, are represented by hooker Brad O'Neill and winger Zach Eckersley.

Leigh centre Umyla Hanley and prop Joe Ofahengaue were rewarded for their form with a pick, with the latter selected alongside Wakefield's Caleb Hamlin-Uele up front in the line-up.

Warrington's Ben Currie was named loose forward, while Toulouse's 16-try Mathieu Jussaume is the Olympique's first Dream Team representative, as a second-row selection.

Connor, Hanley and McDonnell all retain their place from the 2025 selection.

Although pipped to the League Leaders' Shield by Wigan at the tail end of the campaign, Leeds were a consistent force in 2026's regular season.

Their attack accrued more than 900 points, helped by the creativity of reigning Man of Steel Connor, who has 43 try assists to his name.

Likewise, Miller laid on 18 assists to go with 3,781 metres and a competition-best 166 tackle busts, and Croft, who contributed 12, as well as a personal 28 tries in all competitions.

Explosive winger Sivo was on course to smash records when he stormed to 31 tries in 20 games before a broken arm halted his progress, and the provider for a good chunk of those was his centre partner Handley, who finished with 14 assists and 10 tries.

McDonnell's industry in the back row helped sway his selection, with 651 tackles, 222 carries, and a useful 12 tries marking his contribution.

England head coach Brian McDermott can be heartened by the number of England-qualified players in the Dream Team, given that the 2026 World Cup is little over a month away.

O'Neill put last season's Grand Final sin-binning and disappointment of defeat behind him in 2026 to show he is of international quality, adding a run threat to his excellent defence [894 tackles this season] and distribution from dummy-half.

His club-mate Eckersley not only offers versatility across the backline, having played centre and full-back at times in 2026, but also scored 36 tries in 31 games in all competitions, running almost 3,000 metres and making 30 clean breaks.

Wakefield's Auckland-born Hamlin-Uele, who qualifies via his grandparents, was an immense force for Trinity up front, surpassing 3,000 metres, crushing out 78 tackle busts and contributing 751 tackles in defence.

Rhinos three-quarter Handley was another included in McDermott's 40-strong pool of talent named earlier this year, as was Hanley at Leigh, who, despite missing a chunk of the campaign through injury, still managed to notch 10 try assists, 65 tackle busts and 12 clean breaks.

Another of those selections, Currie, has been typically consistent for Warrington this year, making 933 tackles and taking 349 hit-ups for 2,333 metres.

Wigan's impressive spine of Jai Field, Bevan French and Harry Smith would have been involved in the conversation for the Dream Team and might still have a say in the Man of Steel for their efforts in steering the Cherry and Whites to silverware.

Centre Adam Keighran was another player to have had a claim for selection, as perhaps could Oli Partington in the pack at loose forward and Junior Nsemba in the second row.

Wakefield hooker Tyson Smoothy has been excellent in his one season in the Super League, prior to his return to the NRL next year, but missed out.

Leigh's Josh Charnley has been a regular scorer, moving ahead of Ryan Hall at the top of the all-time Super League tries leaderboard, while half-back Lachlan Lam was influential throughout the campaign with 19 assists alongside Adam Cook.

articles.body: La selección femenina de XV perdió este domingo ante Fiji por 32-38 en el primer encuentro de las WXV Global Series Challenger que se disputa en el Kai Tak Youth Sports Ground de Hong Kong, en el que se desfondó en el último tramo y dejó escapar una importante ventaja ante un equipo teóricamente superior, con dos puestos por delante en el ranking de World Rugby. El conjunto dirigido por Regis Sonnes, que comenzó por detrás en el marcador debido a un ensayo temprano del potente cuadro oceánico por medio de Atelaite Buna Ralivanawa, reaccionó y llegó a dominar mediado el segundo periodo por trece puntos (32-19), pero no pudo con el arreón final de sus rivales. articles.title: South Africa v New Zealand: What did we learn from Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series?
articles.summary: What did we learn from South Africa's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series victory over New Zealand?
articles.body:
South Africa further cemented themselves as the world's best team with a 3-1 victory over New Zealand in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series.

After losing the opening Test in Johannesburg, the world champions won three straight games, comfortably claiming the series with a 43-28 win in Baltimore.

The fourth Test, played in the United States, came after three Tests in South Africa where the All Blacks continued to show promising signs under Dave Rennie.

With the Rugby World Cup next year, what did we learn from the series, which replaced this year's Rugby Championship and will be played again in 2029?

New Zealander Tony Brown's arrival as attack coach in 2024 pointed to South Africa's ambition to dominate in all facets of the game.

The former Highlanders head coach, who will join the All Blacks in 2028, is known for creating a cohesive attacking shape built on sharp ball movement.

But having been outscored in terms of tries over the first two Tests, the Springboks flipped their pack-power trump card - pivotal to their back-to-back World Cup successes - to prevent a repeat of New Zealand's victorious 1996 series win in South Africa.

Nothing illustrated that more than a monster maul that started just inside New Zealand's 22 and ended with Malcolm Marx peeling off to score the decisive try under the posts.

That came after a penalty try from a scrum in the first half. In Baltimore, their power again proved too much.

"South Africa have tried to play expansively a couple of times when we have dominance after hurting teams in the maul or scrum," Schalk Brits, a 2019 World Cup winner, told BBC Sport.

"New Zealand didn't have that dominance in the forwards, but people said they played beautiful rugby. I don't care if it is beautiful or not.

"Beauty is in the eye of the beholder and I love a maul and scrum."

Fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, who was injured at the end of May, returned to start all four Tests. He was initially named on the bench for the second match, only for Handre Pollard to withdraw.

Despite improving as the series went on, the 24-year-old lacked his usual flashes of individual brilliance.

It remains to be seen whether South Africa turn back to 32-year-old Pollard, as they did in 2023, on the biggest occasions to close out games.

Rassie Erasmus' experienced back-to-back World Cup winners - Marx (32), Eben Etzebeth (34), Pieter-Steph du Toit (34), Siya Kolisi (35), Damian de Allende (34), Cheslin Kolbe (32) - all remain regular starters.

The world champions have proven they can also play an exciting brand of attacking rugby, but appeasing the masses will not matter if a familiar formula can bring them three straight World Cups.

All Blacks return to what made them great

Scott Robertson's dismissal in January after two years as head coach sunk New Zealand to a new low.

Rennie, not the flashiest appointment, had to hit the ground running, and a stunning Test win over South Africa at Ellis Park was a case of doing just that.

The 33-16 victory injected jeopardy into a series which many had the Springboks winning comfortably, given their home advantage and recent dominance.

Hurricanes half-backs Cam Roigard and Ruben Love, both aged 25, were trusted by Rennie to instil a return to the All Blacks way - the ability to score from transition from anywhere on the field and compound scoreboard pressure.

Four or more tries in each Test in South Africa showed just that, with the third Test all square at half-time.

"Scott Robertson was a good culture coach but maybe not a brilliant technical coach. Dave Rennie is a brilliant technical coach," former England wing Ugo Monye told Rugby Union Weekly.

"After the Nations Championship, you could see the structures and how they want to play. I think the All Blacks' backline is the most skilled in World Rugby."

Love struggled to have the same commanding impact in Tests two and three, with fly-half Richie Mo'unga returning for the Baltimore game, his first Test since the World Cup final.

The 32-year-old Mo'unga, who is back after a stint in Japan, was not at the standard that made him one of the best fly-halves at the 2023 World Cup.

However, getting him back up to speed will be an All Blacks goal over the next 12 months.

Former England scrum-half Danny Care said: "Imagine what New Zealand would do with a platform and some dominance. It is great for the game that they are coming back to be the All Blacks of old, and the next 12 months will be fascinating."

World Cup rivals: France 'can play multiple styles', and be 'careful of Ireland'

South Africa live for must-win games. That is when, according to Brits, the Boks "come alive".

Defeat at Ellis Park cost them their world number one status - which was quickly regained - but also exposed a vulnerability.

South Africa, who lost matches in the pool stages of the past two World Cups, are currently the favourites to win next year's tournament in Australia, bringing a pressure they have not experienced previously.

"We hate being the favourite, we almost have to have our backs against the wall," Brits said.

"We prefer not to have the eyes on us and move under the radar. I think that is the best way for any team."

Back-to-back Six Nations champions France sent a weakened side to Christchurch in July and lost 34-32 to New Zealand.

When matched against the Springboks last November, France were beaten emphatically, 32-17.

Brits believes France are "the most settled" and offer tactical flexibility similar to that of the world champions.

"I feel like South Africa have an advantage as they can play multiple styles, and it feels like most other nations don't have that capability," Brits said.

"The only team that can play multiple styles is France, as they can grind it out with the forwards, play the kicking game and the expansive game as well."

He added that England still need to become what they are "supposed to be" and to keep an eye on Ireland, who are travelling "under the radar" after peaking in previous World Cup cycles prior to the tournament.

"Ireland still have amazing rugby players and coaches – the best coaches out there - and a top-four squad," Brits added. "Be careful of Ireland."

articles.title: WXV: Megan Davey reignites international ambitions with Wales
articles.summary: Uncapped Wales scrum-half Megan Davey's admits she almost called it quits before her recent call-up at the age of 26.
articles.body:
Megan Davey's international ambitions have been reignited at her self-proclaimed 'old' age of 26.

Loughborough Lightning's record appearance holder considered going into full-time teaching when she did not make Wales' 2026 Six Nations squad.

Her hopes were dashed again when omitted from Sean Lynn's extended training squad for the WXV Global Series.

"There was a little bit of a wobble," admitted uncapped Davey.

"It's hard to keep going when you're at my age, you feel old in the game."

"There's always been something inside me, I know I can do it, it's the voice inside my head that's kept me going," she said.

"I was really happy that I got an opportunity."

Davey qualifies for Wales through her grandfather from Llanelli but went through the English pathway system as a youngster.

"The avenue for under-20s was always really with England because it wasn't as set up with Wales, but now it's really good," she said.

"I'm a little bit older...now I feel like I can really do people proud."

And despite being a latecomer in camp, Davey says everyone has been welcoming.

"There's always that thing when you walk into an environment that's already established, you're like 'how am I going to do?' but I was really raring to go," she added.

"Obviously a bit sad that I wasn't in the squad to begin with, but you just crack on with what you're doing."

Live on BBC One, iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app, with live text coverage

Davey has primarily trained at scrum-half with Wales and faces competition from Keira Bevan and Seren Lockwood.

And contrary to the stereotype of the position, the nines get along with no animosity.

"We all really enjoy each other's company. We want each other to do well, so there's never that hatred towards each other," said Davey, who has previously started at fly-half for Loughborough.

"Whoever goes out there and does the job first is the best pick for the team and you just need to back that completely."

Wales open their WXV campaign against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday, 18 September (19:15 BST), and any potential involvement would mean the world to Davey.

"Playing international rugby is such a privilege and I want to make everyone proud - my family, but also the coaches that have been behind me for the last 15 years of my journey," she said.

"It's just that final step, like 'I made it'. I'm really excited and hopefully it comes at some point."

articles.title: WRU call to cut region not due to women's rugby, says exec Nadine Griffiths
articles.summary: The director of women's rugby at the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has hit back at "embarrassing" claims over why a men's region is being axed.
articles.body:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has hit back at claims the women's programme is a financial drain on the men's game.

WRU women's rugby director Nadine Griffiths said allegations she had read on social media that a region is to be cut because of investment in the women's game were "embarrassing".

And she added the women's game had in fact made money for the governing body.

The Union has had a professional women's programme since the start of 2022 and there are now more than 40 contracted players.

But plans to axe one of the four men's professional regions - most likely Scarlets or Ospreys - has stirred hostility.

"I'm really disappointed and slightly embarrassed by some of the comments I read online about the women's game taking money from the men's game," she said.

"It doesn't. There are five different budget lines, including the men, women, [Principality] stadium and community game."

Griffiths appointed WRU director of women’s rugby

WRU keen for two Welsh sides to join PWR

Griffiths added the women's game generated £1.7m last year and, compared with the men's side of the sport, has more potential for commercial growth.

"If we look at the men's game we are hitting ceilings in terms of where our commercial growth opportunities are, there's only so much more we can charge for tickets, there's only so many people we can get into the ground," Griffiths said.

"Our women's game is a growth area and provides us an opportunity to really bring in some serious cash into Welsh rugby as a whole.

"It's bringing people who don't traditionally watch rugby and again it leads into that commercial growth where we're selling more jerseys and watching more games. So it actually lends into growing Welsh rugby as a whole."

Griffiths has been in post since June and is part of the WRU's executive team.

Her current priority for the women's game is visibility - building the profile of not only the senior team, but also pathways and grassroots rugby.

She accepts that is not helped by the miserable current form of the the senior side who are without a win in their last nine Test matches and have slumped to an all time low of 13th in the world.

"We can't hide from the fact that results matter," said the former international.

"The litmus test will be the WXV competition. It gives us a brilliant opportunity to test our progress playing against three sides that are ranked higher than us."

Wales open their campaign against South Africa on Friday at Cardiff Arms Park (19:15 BST) and play USA at the same venue eight days later. They then travel to Japan for two Tests in October.

"[Results] are not going to come overnight, we're building a house and we have to build those foundations," Griffiths said, pointing to encouraging results from the under-18s and under-21s sides.

Head coach Sean Lynn also selected eight uncapped players in his WXV squad.

"It shows us that our pathways are working. When they are working and you've built that competition for places, eventually results will come."

articles.title: Henry Pollock: Northampton star 'open to offers' as contract talks continue
articles.summary: Henry Pollock continues to play hardball in his negotiations over a Northampton Saints contract extension, insisting he is still open to offers from elsewhere.
articles.body:
Henry Pollock continues to play hardball in his negotiations over a Northampton Saints contract extension, insisting he is still open to offers from elsewhere, including overseas, and that he remains determined to be "quite selfish" over his future.

The 21-year-old England back row's current deal, thought to be worth about £150,000 a year, expires at the end of the forthcoming campaign.

Pollock added Eddie Hearn to his advisory team earlier this year and the boxing impresario upped the ante by claiming his new client was "a seven-figure player", whose current pay shocked him.

"Northampton's been so great to me, I've been here my whole career and they've made me who I am. For me to stay here would be so special," said Pollock.

"Obviously, I know it's not as easy as that and I know there's lots of moving parts that come into play. I'm very open to new opportunities and I'm very open to exploring that.

"I'm so young so I think it's only right that I assess those options and find the best decision for myself."

He added: "Your career is so short that you look back on yourself and you almost regret not exploring new avenues, exploring different things.

"I think for me, you almost have to be quite selfish in that aspect, think what's right for you. If that is staying here, then that's great, I'll be here for however long. If it's not, then I'll be open to new opportunities."

Salary cap rules, which prevent players moving between Prem clubs from being designated as 'marquee' players whose pay is exempt from a £6.4m squad limit, make a big-money move to one of Saints' domestic rivals difficult.

A move to a club in France or Japan would potentially be lucrative to Pollock, and a deal which began at the start of the 2027-28 season would not rule him out of contention for England's Rugby World Cup squad next autumn.

However, he would become ineligible for England once he begins playing overseas and would lose the central contract, worth about £150,000 a year, that currently tops up his club wages.

His off-pitch earnings - he has personal endorsement deals with various clothing brands - might also suffer away from the exposure of the Test arena and domestic rugby.

"I definitely want to go and live in different countries, explore new sports, explore new avenues," said Pollock.

"Again, that's all down to the management team. I'm just speaking to them loads and assessing my options and seeing what's right for myself."

Saints allowed club captain George Furbank to leave for Harlequins in the summer, conscious that a raft of young stars in their title-winning team were due a pay rise.

Fly-half Fin Smith agreed a new deal in October, while wing Tommy Freeman is in line for his own new deal this season. Scrum-half Archie McParland and prop Emmanuel Iyogun are also priorities to tie down to new contracts.

"We're getting closer," said director of rugby Phil Dowson on a deal with Pollock.

"As you can imagine, it's complex. There's a few moving parts that we need to put together, but I'm hopeful. As I said before, he wants to stay and we want to keep him.

"Obviously there's some negotiations going between that but those two things are very positive."

articles.title: Ronan O'Gara: La Rochelle head coach signs contract extension until 2031
articles.summary: La Rochelle head coach Ronan O'Gara signs a contract extension to keep him at the club until 2031.
articles.body:
La Rochelle head coach Ronan O'Gara has signed a contract extension to keep him at the club until 2031.

O'Gara arrived at the club in 2019 after coaching spells with rival Top 14 side Racing 92 and New Zealand outfit Crusaders.

Following defeat in the 2021 European Champions Cup final, the former Ireland international signed an initial extension before guiding La Rochelle to back-to-back final wins in 2022 and 2023 - the club's first major silverware.

"My family and I are very happy and proud to continue this adventure with Stade Rochelais," O'Gara told the club website.

"We have lived through exceptional times and gone through more difficult times together. In each of them, I felt the confidence of the club and the support of our supporters.

"I believe deeply in this club, in its players, in its staff and in its ambition. We have already built a lot of things, but I am convinced that the best is still ahead of us.

"I want to continue to grow this team and win with Stade Rochelais."

La Rochelle have made a winning start to the new Top 14 season, defeating Toulouse on the opening weekend before a 21-20 away win in Toulon on Saturday.

They return to action this Saturday against Racing 92.

Last season, La Rochelle finished sixth in the Top 14 to secure a return to the Investec Champions Cup before bowing out of their domestic play-offs at the quarter-final stage at the hands of Stade Francais.

In Europe, they dropped into the Challenge Cup where they were eliminated by Ulster in the quarter-finals.

articles.title: Henry Pollock: Northampton Saints star open to exploring opportunities in future and says Eddie Hearn's £1m valuation 'isn't a pressure'
articles.summary: Henry Pollock's contract with Northampton expires in summer 2027; Pollock's agent Eddie Hearn says the England forward merits a salary of more than £1m per year; Pollock says he is open to exploring all options
articles.body:
Pollock's focus remains on rugby and he is at the advanced stage of negotiations for a new contract with Gallagher Prem champions Northampton.

However, the 21-year-old is also looking to eventually broaden his horizons having signed for Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency.

"I definitely want to go and live in different countries, explore new sports, explore new avenues," Pollock said.

"Eddie and the Matchroom team are constantly messaging me, calling me about different avenues and they've been great with that kind of stuff. I'm not going to say no to any opportunity.

"At the minute rugby is my main priority so I'm focusing on that in the near future, but as I said, you never know what's happening around the corner."

Hearn told Northampton in August that Pollock is "certainly a seven-figure player" because of the commercial clout he brings and the Lions flanker has taken the £1m-plus valuation in his stride.

"I don't see it as pressure," he said. "I see it as him doing his job. He's the best sports promoter in the world. The reason he's the best is because he gets his client what he deserves.

"Eddie's been great for me and he's given me so many avenues to get into. The way that he can give me access to loads of different stuff has been amazing.

"I have no bad words about him. The sport of rugby needs to change and hopefully this is a change."

While Pollock's options for his future remain vast, it is understood that he is close to remaining at Northampton.

While Pollock wants to remain at a club that has been "special" to him, he understands that, during his career, he may need to make "selfish" decisions for his trajectory.

"Northampton's been so great to me, I've been here my whole career and they've made me who I am. For me to stay here would be so special," said Pollock.

"Obviously, I know it's not as easy as that and I know there's lots of moving parts that come into play. I'm very open to new opportunities and I'm very open to exploring that.

"I'm so young so I think it's only right that I assess those options and find the best decision for myself.

"Your career is so short that you look back on yourself and you almost regret not exploring new avenues, exploring different things," he later added.

"I think for me, you almost have to be quite selfish in that aspect, think what's right for you. If that is staying here, then that's great, I'll be here for however long. If it's not, then I'll be open to new opportunities."

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup: Brian McDermott wants to commit to England for 2030
articles.summary: Brian McDermott says he wants to stay on as England's head coach for the 2030 Rugby League World Cup.
articles.body:
Brian McDermott says he wants to stay on as England's head coach for the 2030 Rugby League World Cup.

The former Leeds Rhinos head coach, 56, was appointed on a short-term agreement in April to guide England through this autumn's World Cup, which is taking place in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea.

McDermott said when he started in the job that he would be interested in staying on beyond the tournament.

And although he has made clear that he wants to focus on the immediate task of seeking success this October and November, he does want to commit to his country for the long term if all goes well.

He said: "Well, we've had a very informal discussion about what that might look like and then that's all it is. And it's been a really short conversation.

"Clearly, I'd like to do the job for longer. I'd like to get another crack at the World Cup in four years' time.

"You know, if you're going to do this properly, give me four years' preparation, where we're building it up year by year and getting players connected to a programme which has got a start, a middle and the end."

McDermott, currently working as an assistant coach at NRL club Gold Coast Titans, has taken the England role on a part-time basis, in contrast to his full-time predecessor Shaun Wane.

He has confirmed Wigan great Sean O'Loughlin and St Helens legend Paul Wellens as assistant coaches for the World Cup.

And he believes England are well set for it, but having had only a limited time to prepare - with no matches before their World Cup opener against Tonga in Perth on 17 October - he would like a chance to have a full build-up to a major tournament.

He said: "This has been a crazy, crazy period over the last few months to try and coordinate all this. And I think we're in good shape, by the way.

"But yeah, I've made it no secret. I'd like a crack at the next World Cup and a four-year build-up to that.

"We haven't gone too deep into those discussions. And when you mention it, you think, no, let's not talk about that. I've got to get my mind on this here. So it has been mentioned, but I'm not chasing that just yet."

New England boss McDermott offers route back for Connor

Rhinos dominate 2026 Super League Dream Team

McDermott said when he took the job that he intended to stick with George Williams as captain.

The Warrington half-back, who will leave Super League for NRL club Dolphins after the World Cup, returned to action in August after four months out with a neck injury.

Having got to know Williams during that time, McDermott is happy to have him leading the team.

"He's been great to speak to," McDermott said. "I didn't really know George at all.

"It's been really enjoyable to get to know him. He's keen as anything.

"And while he was injured, you could just tell he came back from injury early, but you could tell if there's anybody who's going to come back from it early, it would be him.

"And I'm really pleased to see the form that he's in now.

"His leadership's been really good. When we've had the groups meetings, I saw the way he would speak on there and just have a bit of maturity.

articles.title: George Williams: England coach Brian McDermott confirms Warrington Wolves star as captain for Rugby League World Cup
articles.summary: George Williams will captain England at the upcoming Rugby League World Cup which leaves a dilemma for head coach Brian McDermott; watch Wakefield Trinity vs Leigh Leopards in the Super League Eliminators, live on Sky Sports on Friday September 18, with kick-off at 8pm
articles.body:
Williams suffered a neck injury and required surgery in April but returned to action in August and has hit the ground running for Warrington Wolves since, hoping to lead them to the Super League Grand Final.

Warrington face Hull KR in the eliminators this Saturday, live on Sky Sports , with the winner facing Wigan Warriors in the semi-finals before the Grand Final on October 3.

McDermott has been impressed with Williams' return from injury and said his "leadership has been really good".

"I didn't really know George at all. In fact, I didn't know many of the squad at all, to be fair. I've only ever shook their hands after games," he said.

"I normally shook George's hand after his team beat my team when I was at Leeds. We had a horrible record against Wigan in the regular season!

"It's been really enjoyable to get to know him. He's keen as anything and while he was injured, you could tell if anyone was coming back from injury early then it would be him.

"I'm pleased to see the form he's in now, the intent he's playing. He's not feathering about on his feet and waiting for the game to come to him, he's going and getting the game. He goes and chases the game and that's George Williams all over.

"When he first broke into first grade, we all said, 'who the hell's this guy?' Because he went and got the game, he chased the game, whether he's trying to beat the bloke opposite him or quite often coming back to the inside and finding a lazy defender. Add a few years to that and he's got a bit stronger and wiser."

Williams being captain means he will almost certainly take one of the half-back spots, which raises question marks over who will partner him.

Mikey Lewis, Jake Connor, Harry Smith and Hugo Savala are all in the mix but McDermott suggested only three will be on the plane to the World Cup, which takes place in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea from October 15 to November 15.

"Whether we take a six and a seven to back up the six and a seven that I have in mind to start, I'm still not sure," said McDermott.

"We're certainly going to take another half. We need to take another half. But if we take two halves as cover, it has an impact on how many covers we have for our outside backs, what cover we have with the back rowers, what cover we have for the other spine members as well. Some of that will be to do with form, some of that will be to do with versatility as well.

"If a guy can play in the halves, but he can also play at nine, I might favour that as well. Unsure yet. Certainly, the spine members there, it's a difficult one with the spine members.

"I've got to see them play in finals. Everyone would understand who the spine members are going to be or what other players I'm choosing from. But there's another couple out there that the finals will reveal.

"Can they handle the big occasion? Can they handle the game when there's so much on the balance? I'll certainly be taking one half as back-up. Whether I take two or not, it's dependent on the ship."

articles.title: Wales injury blow as Harlequins' Kayleigh Powell ruled out of WXV
articles.summary: Wales have been dealt another injury blow ahead of their WXV Global Series with Kayleigh Powell ruled out of the entire campaign.
articles.body:
Wales have been dealt another injury blow before their WXV Global Series campaign with Harlequins' Kayleigh Powell ruled out of the entire tournament.

The 27-year-old sevens Olympian was a standout player at full-back during the Six Nations and impressed at fly-half when Wales ended their nine match losing streak against the Barbarians in June.

But she will sit out Wales' Tests against South Africa, USA and Japan after suffering a hamstring injury in training.

Powell wrote on her social media that she was "absolutely gutted" to be missing the campaign, but has "every faith that this team will do great things."

Wales open their WXV campaign against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday (19:15 BST) before hosting USA at the same venue eight days later.

The squad will then travel to Japan for two Tests, on 23 and 31 October.

Women's rugby not to blame for region axe - WRU

Wales select eight uncapped players in WXV squad

Wales head coach Sean Lynn said: "Kayleigh was outstanding against the Barbarians, she brought another dimension to our attack.

"It's a big loss, but it's a big opportunity for individuals who've been training hard this pre-season to step up and enter the international arena."

Lleucu George could slot back in at 10, while scrum-half Keira Bevan provides another option having trained there during pre-season.

"I was really impressed watching Keira play for Bristol Bears against Gloucester-Hartpury at the tail end of the season, she went very well [at 10].

"Myself and [attack coach] Ashley Beck had a conversation with her and she's been slotting in at 10. She's just given us another dimension, another edge to our attack and has been looking really comfortable."

Lynn's squad has taken a battering during pre-season, with Premiership Women's Rugby (PRW) title-winning prop Donna Rose and uncapped centres Kelsie Webster and Hanna Tudor already ruled out.

Lynn said the growing injury list was an indication of the intensity in training.

"We don't want to be where we are ranked in the world [13th], we want to be more competitive and we've had to move the dial this pre-season," he said.

"The girls have said it's probably the hardest off-season, and that's what we have to do. It's now about getting depth in our squad, and we're getting that because of the competitive environment."

Backs Carys Cox and Nel Metcalfe have returned to training, but will not be in contention for Friday's opening game.

"Carys started doing some rugby this week and we're hoping she will go back into it again next week. Fingers crossed, and with all boxes ticked, we might see her come off the bench and get some minutes against USA," Lynn said.

"And for Nel, what we'll be looking for is can we take her to Japan?"
